```{r}
numbers <- c(18, 1024, 92, 73, 14)
sum(numbers)
mean(numbers)
sd(numbers) %>% round(digits = 2) # can include 'digits =' but don't need to because r recognizes the order of arguments; round(digits = 2) is the same as round(2)
```

##  Winter Chapter 2

### 2.11.3

```{r}
data_nettle <- read_csv(here("Data", "nettle_1999_climate.csv"))
# show data only for Benin
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country == "Benin")
# show data from Benin and Zaire
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country %in% c("Benin", "Zaire"))
# show only Langs column
data_nettle %>%
  select(Langs)
# show Langs data for Benin
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country == "Benin") %>%
  select(Langs)
# show data for Population to MGS columns for Benin
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Country == "Benin") %>%
  select(Population:MGS)
# return rows where Langs > 200
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Langs > 200)
# return rows where Langs > 200 and Population < median(Population)
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Langs > 200,
         Population < median(Population))
```

### 2.11.4

```{r}
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
   MGS_cat = ifelse(MGS < 6, "dry", "fertile") 
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(LangSum = sum(Langs))

# using case_when
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS >= 6 ~ "fertile",
      .unmatched = "error"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(LangSum = sum(Langs))

# example
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  4 ~ "very dry",
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS <  8 ~ "fertile",
      MGS >= 8 ~ "very fertile",
      .unmatched = "error"
    ),
    MGS_cat = fct_relevel(MGS_cat, "very dry", "dry", "fertile", "very fertile")
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(LangSum = sum(Langs))

# sanity check: does case_when operate the way i think it does
data_nettle %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  4 ~ "very dry",
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS <  8 ~ "fertile",
      MGS >= 8 ~ "very fertile",
      .unmatched = "error")
    ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  count()

# get descriptive statistics for the smallpopulation data
data_nettle %>%
  filter(Population < 4) %>%
  mutate(
    MGS_cat = case_when(
      MGS <  4 ~ "very dry",
      MGS <  6 ~ "dry",
      MGS <  8 ~ "fertile",
      MGS >= 8 ~ "very fertile",
      .unmatched = "error"
    ),
    MGS_cat = fct_relevel(MGS_cat, "very dry", "dry", "fertile", "very fertile")
  ) %>%
  group_by(MGS_cat) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(Langs) %>% round(2),
            sd = sd(Langs) %>% round(2),
            min = min(Langs),
            max = max(Langs))
```

## Winter Chapter 3

```{r}
# generate and plot a normal distribution
rnorm(50) %>%
  hist() # base r

# non-base r version
rnorm(50) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%      # make a data frame
  rename(score = 1) %>%    # rename the variable
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) + # make the plot
  geom_histogram()

# set the mean and sd
rnorm(50, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  hist() 

# with ggplot
rnorm(50, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")

# with 12 participants
rnorm(12, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")
# with 1200
rnorm(1200, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")

# how would we screen / filter scores > 100 and < 0
rnorm(1200, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  filter(score <= 100) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")

# convert to sds
rnorm(1200, 71.82, 10.42) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(score = 1) %>%
  filter(score <= 100) %>%
  mutate(
    score.z = scale(score) # take the z score (standardize)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = score.z)) +
  geom_histogram(color = "black", fill = "white")
```

### Boxplots

```{r}
# valence of words a vs p
library(stringr)
data_war %>%
  mutate(
    word_type = case_when(
      str_detect(Word, "^a") ~ "a",
      str_detect(Word, "^p") ~ "p",
      .default = "error"
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(word_type != "error") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = word_type, y = Val)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()

# creating a valence factor with levels low, medium, high
data_war %>%
  mutate(
    word_type = case_when(
      Val < 3 ~ "low",
      Val < 7 ~ "medium",
      Val >= 7 ~ "high",
      .default = "error"),
    word_type = fct_relevel(word_type, "low", "medium", "high")
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = word_type, y = Val)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Winter Chapter 4

```{r}
# generate predictor
x <- rnorm(50)
# generate outcome
y <- 10 + 3*x
# generate error
error <- rnorm(50)
# remake outcome
y <- 10 + 3*x + error

# make this into a dataframe
df <- tibble(
  predictor = x,
  outcome = y
  )

# fit a regression and get a tidy output
fm <- lm(outcome ~ predictor, df)
tidy(fm)
# rounding to three decimals
tidy(fm) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
# add predicted values to df (predictions for actual observations)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = predict(fm),
    residual = fitted - outcome
  )
# create a new set of values and predict
df_prediction <- tibble(predictor = seq(-3, 3, 0.1))
df_prediction$predicted <- predict(fm, newdata = df_prediction)

# make a plot
ggplot(df, aes(predictor, outcome)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# read, convert variables to lowercase, and inspect the data
data_elp <- read_csv(here("Data", "ELP_frequency.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower)
glimpse(data_elp)
# make log variable
data_elp <- data_elp %>%
  mutate(
    freq.log = log10(freq)
  )
# fit and inspect the model
fm <- lm(rt ~ freq.log, data_elp)
tidy(fm) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
# make a plot
ggplot(data_elp, aes(freq.log, rt)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(data_elp$rt)) +
  theme_minimal()
# how would we label the words?
# how would we fix the resulting plot?
# (prevent words from being cut off)
# (show words on top of the fit line)

# updated plot
ggplot(data_elp, aes(freq.log, rt, label = word)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  geom_label() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(data_elp$rt)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 5)) +
  labs(
    x = "Log10(Frequency)",
    y = "RT"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal()
```

## Data Simulation

```{r}
# simple version with 20 participants and 10 items
# participants
participants <- 20
# items
items <- 10
# groups
groups <- 2
# make a grid (cross everything)
df <- expand.grid(
  participant = factor(1:participants),
  item = factor(1:items),
  group = factor(1:groups)
) %>%
  mutate(
    group = ifelse(group == 1, "a", "b"),
    group.numeric = ifelse(group == "a", 0, 1),
    rt_a = rnorm(400, 500, 100),
    rt_b = rnorm(400, 500, 100),
    rt_b = rt_b - rnorm(400, 10, 10)
    )
df %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = rt, fill = group)) +
  geom_histogram()
min(df$rt)
# how can we simulate different values using rnorm()? done
# how do we add group a vs b? done
# how can we simulate b responds more quickly than a? (1.2x more quickly)
```

## Winter Chapter 5

```{r}
# read the data, convert to lowercase, make the log variables, all in one step
data_elp <- read_csv(here("Data", "ELP_frequency.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(
    freq_log10 = log10(freq),
    rt_log = log(rt)
    )

# make the plots
data_elp %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = freq, y = rt_log, label = word)) +
  geom_text() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_minimal()
data_elp %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = freq_log10, y = rt_log, label = word)) +
  geom_text() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_minimal()

# make and inspect model
fm_elp1 <- lm(rt_log ~ freq_log10, data = data_elp)
tidy(fm_elp1) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )

# store the full intercept and slope using winter's code
b0 <- tidy(fm_elp1)$estimate[1]
b1 <- tidy(fm_elp1)$estimate[2]
# can write a simple function to compute
frequency <- function(x) {
  b0 + b1 * x
}
frequency(1) # 10
frequency(3) # 1000
# predicts on the log scale
# update the function to output raw rt
frequency <- function(x) {
  exp(b0 + b1 * x)
}
frequency(1) # 10
frequency(3) # 1000

# how can we use predict to get the values?
# get predictions for observed values of frequency
data_elp <- data_elp %>%
  mutate(
    fitted = predict(fm_elp1)
  )
# get predictions for specific values
predict(fm_elp1, newdata = data.frame(freq_log10 = c(1, 3, 5))) %>%
  exp()
# make sure to input values based on the predictor's scale
# 1: frequency = 10 (on log10)
# 3: frequency = 1000
# 5: frequency = 100,000
# get predictions for a range of values using seq()
predict(fm_elp1, newdata = data.frame(freq_log10 = seq(1, 3, by = .1))) %>%
  exp() %>%
  round(0) # to get whole numbers, in milliseconds

# create the centered and z-scored variables
data_elp <- data_elp %>%
  mutate(
    freq_log10_c = scale(freq_log10, scale = F),
    freq_log10_z = scale(freq_log10)
  )
# fit the models
fm_elp1_c <- lm(rt_log ~ freq_log10_c, data = data_elp)
fm_elp1_z <- lm(rt_log ~ freq_log10_z, data = data_elp)
tidy(fm_elp1)   %>% dplyr::select(term, estimate)
tidy(fm_elp1_c) %>% dplyr::select(term, estimate)
tidy(fm_elp1_z) %>% dplyr::select(term, estimate)

# get the correlation
data_elp %>%
  select(freq_log10, rt_log) %>%
  cor() %>% round(3)
# suppress the model intercept
lm(scale(rt_log) ~ 0 + freq_log10_z, data_elp) %>%
  tidy() %>%
  select(estimate) %>% round(3)

# next chapter we move to multiple regression:
# y = b0 + b1x + b2x ... + e
# in this chapter, we dealt with frequency
# in the next, we will add word length
# what is the interpretation of the intercept for the following models
# rt ~ frequency + length (frequency = 0 and length = 0, no!)
# rt ~ frequency_c + length_c (frequency = mean(frequency) and length = mean(length))
# rt ~ frequency_c(mean) + length_c(3syllables)
```

## Winter Chapter 6

```{r}
# read the data
data_icon <- read_csv(here("Data", "perry_winter_2017_iconicity.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(
    freq_log10 = log10(freq),
    freq_log10.z = scale(freq_log10),
    ser.z = scale(ser),
    corteseimag.z = scale(corteseimag),
    syst.z = scale(syst)
  )
# inspect it
glimpse(data_icon)

# fit the model with non-standardized variables
fm <- lm(iconicity ~ ser + corteseimag + syst + freq_log10,
   data = data_icon)

# with standardized variables
fm_z <- lm(iconicity ~ ser.z + corteseimag.z + syst.z + freq_log10.z,
   data = data_icon)
glance(fm_z) # r2 does not change
tidy(fm_z) %>% # estimates do
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )

# check assumptions
# plot generates four plots that may be useful to you
plot(fm_z)
# these look fine because nothing is ever perfectly normal

# check for collinearity
# install.packages("car")
car::vif(fm_z) # these are fine (< 4 is desirable)
```

### 6.7.1

```{r}
data_elp <- read_csv(here("Data", "ELP_full_length_frequency.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower) %>%
  mutate(
    freq_log10.z = scale(log10freq),
    length.z = scale(length)
  )

fm_z <- lm(rt ~ freq_log10.z + length.z,
           data = data_elp)
# check assumptions
plot(fm_z) # not good
# vif
car::vif(fm_z)
# inspect estimates
tidy(fm_z)

# what can we do about the assumptions
# plot the data
ggplot(data_elp, aes(log10freq, rt)) +
  # geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", linetype = "dashed") +
  stat_smooth() + # some nonlinearity
  theme_minimal()
ggplot(data_elp, aes(length, rt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.01) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", linetype = "dashed") +
  stat_smooth() + # mostly linear
  theme_minimal()
# try a polynomial predictor for frequency
data_elp <- data_elp %>%
  mutate(
    freq_log10.quad = poly(log10freq, 2)
  )
# refit and check
fm_z2 <- lm(rt ~ freq_log10.quad + length.z,
           data = data_elp)
plot(fm_z2) # a bit better in terms of variance but normality of residuals is still a problem
tidy(fm_z2)
# is this model better
anova(fm_z, fm_z2) # yes
# poly creates orthogonal (uncorrelated) polynomials
# can also do this manually
data_elp <- data_elp %>%
  mutate(
    freq_linear = freq_log10.z,
    freq_quad = freq_linear*freq_linear
    )
# refit
fm_z2 <- lm(rt ~ freq_linear + freq_quad + length.z,
           data = data_elp)
tidy(fm_z2) # values are now interpretable on the original scale
# check vif
car::vif(fm_z2)
# make a plot
data_elp <- data_elp %>%
  mutate(
    predicted = predict(fm_z2)
  )
ggplot(data_elp, aes(freq_log10.z, predicted)) +
  stat_smooth() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "log10(frequency)", y = "reaction time")
# tell me what this is actually predicting? 
# are we predicting the effect of frequency when length = 0 (the mean word length)?
```

## Winter Chapter 7

```{r}
data_senses <- read_csv(here("Data", "winter_2016_senses_valence.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower)
glimpse(data_senses)

# tabulate how many words per modality
# histogram by modality

# only smell and taste words
data_ts <- data_senses %>%
  filter(modality %in% c("Taste", "Smell"))
table(data_ts$modality)
data_ts %>%
  group_by(modality) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(val), sd = sd(val)) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2)
    )
  )

# plots
data_ts %>%
  ggplot(aes(modality, val, fill = modality)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  theme_minimal()
# violin
data_ts %>%
  ggplot(aes(modality, val, fill = modality)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0, width = 0.1, shape = 21) +
  theme_minimal()

# treatment model
fm_treat <- lm(val ~ modality, data_ts)
fm_treat %>% tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )

# predictions
ts_preds <- tibble(modality = unique(data_ts$modality))
ts_preds$fit <- predict(fm_treat, ts_preds)

# change the reference and refit
data_ts <- data_ts %>%
  mutate(
    modality = fct_relevel(modality, c("Taste", "Smell"))
  )
lm(val ~ modality, data_ts) %>%
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
# same value but negative

# add a new sum-coded variable
data_ts <- data_ts %>%
  mutate(
    modality_sum = modality,
  )
contrasts(data_ts$modality_sum) <- contr.sum(2)
fm_sum <- lm(val ~ modality_sum, data_ts)
fm_sum %>% tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
# why is the estimate for modality_sum1 half of the estimate of modality from the treatment-coded model?
# how might we address that, if we wanted to?
# add a contrast-coded variable
data_ts <- data_ts %>%
  mutate(
    modality_contrast = ifelse(modality == "Smell", -.5, .5)
  )
lm(val ~ modality_contrast, data_ts) %>% 
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )

# all senses
fm_all <- lm(val ~ modality, data_senses)
fm_all %>% tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
# can compute by hand or use predict
sense_preds <- tibble(modality = sort(unique(data_senses$modality)))
sense_preds$fit <- round(predict(fm_all, sense_preds), 3)
# assumptions
plot(fm_all)

# what if we sum-coded all five senses?
contr.sum(5)
data_senses <- data_senses %>%
  mutate(
    modality_sum = as.factor(modality),
  )
contrasts(data_senses$modality_sum) <- contr.sum(5)
fm_all <- lm(val ~ modality_sum, data_senses)
fm_all %>% tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
# what do the estimates represent?
# hint: look at the contr.sum(5) matrix
data_senses %>%
  group_by(modality) %>%
  summarize(
    mean = mean(val) %>% round(2)
  )
```

### 7.12.2 

```{r}
lyn <- read_csv(here("Data", "lynott_connell_2009_modality.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower)
icon <- read_csv(here("Data", "perry_winter_2017_iconicity.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower)
# merge
data_iconicity <- left_join(lyn, icon)
glimpse(data_iconicity)
fm_iconicity <- lm(iconicity ~ dominantmodality, data_iconicity)
fm_iconicity %>% tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
# intercept = ?
# get categories (my way)
icon_preds <- data_iconicity %>%
  distinct(dominantmodality) %>%
  arrange(dominantmodality)
icon_preds$fit <- round(predict(fm_iconicity, icon_preds), 3)
# how closely do these match the means?
means <- data_iconicity %>%
  group_by(dominantmodality) %>%
  summarize(
    mean = mean(iconicity, na.rm = T) %>% round(3)
  )
# add these to tibble
icon_preds <- icon_preds %>%
  left_join(means)
icon_preds # perfect match, which makes sense because with one categorical predictor, the prediction is the mean per category
```

```{r}
# categorical * categorical

# when in doubt, write the equation

# references
# semantically different = 0 (reference)
# phonologically different = 0 (reference)
# semantically similar = 1
# phonologically similar = 1

# equation
# distance = intercept + b1*sem + b2*phon + b3*phon*sem
# sem-d, phon-d; distance = intercept
# sem-d, phon-s; distance = intercept + phon
# sem-s, phon-d; distance = intercept + sem
# sem-s, phon-s; distance = intercept + phon + sem + phon*sem

sem <- rep(c("different", "similar"), times = 2)
data_new <- tibble(phon, sem)

data_new

    sem_contrast = ifelse(sem == "Different", -0.5, 0.5)

# sum

    )
  )
# contrast
fm_4.2 <- lm(distance ~ phon_contrast*sem_contrast, data_sim)
tidy(fm_4.2) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )
```

### 9.9.3

```{r}
n <- 10
meandiff <- 2
my_sd <- 2
t.test(
  rnorm(n, sd = my_sd),
  rnorm(n, sd = my_sd) + meandiff
)

# write a simple function to run this repeatedly
run_ttest <- function(reps, n, my_sd, meandiff) {
  results <- data.frame(t = numeric(reps), p = numeric(reps))

  for (i in 1:reps) {
    test <- t.test(
      rnorm(n, sd = my_sd),
      rnorm(n, sd = my_sd) + meandiff
    )
    results$t[i] <- test$statistic
    results$p[i] <- test$p.value
  }

  results
}

# run it with Winter's values
run_ttest(reps = 100, n = 28, my_sd = .12, meandiff = .50) %>%
  mutate(
    significant = ifelse(p < .05, "yes", "no")
  ) %>%
  count(significant)
# yes / no
#  60 / 40
#. 58 / 42
#. 49 / 51

# estimate power based on standardized effect size
# install.packages("pwr")
# mean estimate
pwr::pwr.t.test(
  d = .50,
  sig.level = .05,
  power = .80,
  type = "two.sample"
  ) # 64 per group
# smallest estimate
pwr::pwr.t.test(
  d = .25,
  sig.level = .05,
  power = .80,
  type = "two.sample"
  ) # 253 per group

# what about within subjects
pwr::pwr.t.test(
  d = .50,
  sig.level = .05,
  power = .80,
  type = "paired"
  ) # 34
pwr::pwr.t.test(
  d = .25,
  sig.level = .05,
  power = .80,
  type = "paired"
  ) # 128
```

```{r}
  mutate(
```

### 11.3

```{r}
data_senses <- read_csv(here("Data", "winter_2016_senses_valence.csv")) %>%
  rename_with(tolower)

fm_senses <- lm(val ~ modality, data_senses)

tidy(fm_senses) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )

# create a null model for model comparisons
fm_senses_0 <- lm(val ~ 1, data_senses)
# compare the models
anova(fm_senses_0, fm_senses)
# adding modality significantly improves the fit of the model
# why does df = 4 in this output?

# this tells you the variable is an important predictor
# it doesn't tell you anything about pairwise comparisons by modality

# need emmeans for that
# install.packages("emmeans")
library(emmeans)
emmeans(fm_senses, pairwise ~ modality, adjust = "bonferroni")
# caution: in many cases, it doesn't make sense to run all comparisons
# can get the specific comparisons that you want (better approach)
```

### 11.4

```{r}
# winter's approach
data_senses <- data_senses %>%
  mutate(
    val_z = scale(val),
    val_abs = abs(val_z)
  )

fm_senses_abs <- lm(val_abs ~ modality, data_senses)
anova(fm_senses_abs)

# taste/smell and sight/sound/touch
data_senses <- data_senses %>%
  mutate(
    chemvsrest = ifelse(modality %in% c("Taste", "Smell"), "Chem", "Other")
  )
with(data_senses, table(modality, chemvsrest))
fm_senses_abs <- lm(val_abs ~ chemvsrest, data_senses)
tidy(fm_senses_abs) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  ) %>% print()

# alternative approach: set specific contrasts
# get the grid
fm_senses_abs <- lm(val_abs ~ modality, data_senses)
grid_senses <- emmeans(fm_senses_abs, ~ modality) # returns order of predictors
# look at the reference grid
grid_senses
# build a grid of contrasts
contrasts_senses <- list(
  smellvstaste = c(0, -1, 0, 1, 0),
  chemvsother  = c(-1/3, 1/2, -1/3, 1/2, -1/3)
)
# run contrasts
contrast(grid_senses, contrasts_senses) # returns unadjusted p values
contrast(grid_senses, contrasts_senses, adjust = "bonferroni")

# check estimates
# contrast approach:  0.265, SE = 0.084
# winter's approach: -0.342, SE = 0.080
# why the difference?
# 1. sign is different because in model, other - chem; contrast, chem - other
# 2. estimate is different because of unbalanced n (model is weighted by n)
data_senses %>%
  group_by(modality) %>%
  count()
```

```{r}

# manual confidence interval
ci_tib <- tibble(fits, ses) %>%
  mutate(

    ub = fits + 1.96 *ses

  round(3)
ci_tib
```

```{r}
# formula

# predicted probability for bac = 0.3
plogis((-3.64 + 16.12 * .3)) * 100 # 76.78%

# make a prediction
bac_vals <- seq(0, 0.4, 0.01)
y_preds <- predict(fm_alcohol, newdata = data.frame(bac = bac_vals))
predictions <- tibble(bac_vals, y_preds) %>%
  mutate(probs = plogis(y_preds))
ggplot(data_alcohol, aes(bac, speech_error)) +
  # plot the observed data using geom_jitter() to stagger points
  geom_jitter(size = 4, alpha = 0.6, height = 0.05) +
  # plot the prediction
  geom_line(data = predictions, aes(bac_vals, probs)) +
  theme_minimal()
```
